name: stats-explorer-mcp
displayName: Stats Explorer MCP: Verified Statistics for AI Agents
description: Statistics and analytics tools for Copilot and Claude: t-tests, ANOVA, chi-square, correlation, group summaries and "what drives X", with effect sizes, confidence intervals and plain-English results. Any file size. Runs locally.

commands.title: Copy MCP Config for Other Editors
Copy Setup Command for Claude Code
Copy Setup Commands for Claude Code (with Jev)
Add Jev Routing Instructions to This Workspace
Set TypeSafe API Key (for Jev enforce mode)

statsExplorer.dataFolders.description: Extra folders the statistics tools may read data files from. Open workspace folders are always allowed.

statsExplorer.guidedWorkflow.markdownDescription: Guide the AI through Stats Explorer's workflow: it first decides whether your request needs a hypothesis test or just exploration, and hypothesis tests follow the six *Bring it all together* steps in order. Turn off to give the AI the individual test tools directly.

enumDescriptions: Editable forms (Copilot in VS Code shows these)
A message in the chat that you answer by replying

statsExplorer.confirmSelections.markdownDescription: Ask you to confirm every column, group, chart type and report section the AI picks (as dropdowns you can change) before anything runs.

enumDescriptions: No orchestrator: Copilot/Claude call your Jev MCP server with packets Stats Explorer prepares, then record the answer
Stats Explorer calls the Jev API itself (set the key with "Stats Explorer: Set TypeSafe API Key"); the AI can't skip or alter the checks
statsExplorer.jev.mode.markdownDescription: Have **Jev** (TypeSafe's judgment model) independently check the test plan and the AI's written conclusions against the computed results. For production pipelines with an orchestrator, run the server with `STATS_EXPLORER_JEV=orchestrated` instead ([docs](https://github.com/meador793/stats-explorer-mcp/blob/main/docs/JEV.md)).

statsExplorer.jev.checkpoints.markdownDescription: Where Jev checks: `plan` (step 1 of a hypothesis test), `conclusions` (the AI's finding sentences), `data` (screens column names and text values in data files for instructions aimed at an AI; sends text samples to Jev).

statsExplorer.jev.waitForJev.markdownDescription: Cooperate mode: a checkpoint waits until the AI has recorded Jev's answer. Off = the check is only suggested.

statsExplorer.jev.passAt.description: A check passes when Jev's probability that it is fine is at least this.

statsExplorer.jev.failBelow.description: A check fails below this probability; in between, it is flagged for review.

statsExplorer.jev.auditLog.description: Path of a JSON Lines file that records every Jev checkpoint decision (no data values or keys). Empty = no log.

statsExplorer.largeFiles.streamAboveMB.markdownDescription: CSV, TSV and Parquet files larger than this (in MB) are read in parallel streaming passes instead of being loaded into memory. Any size works, including terabytes; memory doesn't grow with the file (about 0.5 GB plus about 0.2 GB per parallel reader).

statsExplorer.largeFiles.parallelReaders.description: How many CPU cores read a large file at once. 0 = automatic (all cores but one, up to 16).

statsExplorer.largeFiles.askAboveMinutes.description: If reading a whole file would take longer than this, you are asked first whether to read all of it (exact) or a quick sample.

statsExplorer.largeFiles.samplePercent.description: Size of the quick sample, as a percentage of the file, when you choose a sample instead of a full read.

statsExplorer.largeFiles.saveColumns.markdownDescription: After a full read of a large file, keep the columns it read on disk (8 bytes per number, 4 per text value) so follow-up questions on them take seconds. `ask` asks each time.

statsExplorer.largeFiles.cacheFolder.description: Where saved columns are kept. Empty = your system's temporary folder.

statsExplorer.maxFileMB.description: Refuse data files larger than this (in MB). 0 = no limit.

statsExplorer.showAppLink.description: Add a one-line link to the Stats Explorer app at the end of each result.
